🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>CANADIAN HOTEL CHAIN ABANDONS CUBA UNDER US SANCTIONS PRESSURE — 15 PROPERTIES GONE</u>

Blue Diamond — Cuba's third-largest foreign hotel operator with 15 properties under Royalton, Memories, Starfish, Mystique, and Resonance brands across Havana, Varadero, and Cayo Largo — announced immediate exit June 1, hours before a US deadline forcing foreign firms to cut ties with companies "linked to Cuban Armed Forces." French CMA CGM and German Hapag-Lloyd already pulled shipping. Havana now living through 22-hour daily blackouts. The siege keeps tightening. Spanish Meliá and Iberostar (53 hotels combined) haven't moved — yet.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>BRUGADA: WORLD CUP MEXICO IS FOR THE PEOPLE WHO LIVE HERE — NOT JUST TOURISTS</u>

"Vivir el Mundial no solo es al interior del estadio, sino fuera de él," said CDMX Mayor Clara Brugada. The city will run special Metrobús, Trolebús, and Tren Ligero routes to the Estadio Azteca from north, central, and south zones — public transit prioritized over cars, free cultural events around the stadium for non-ticketed residents. Schools close June 11 for Mexico vs South Africa. FIFA's price-gouging machine meets the 4T's right-to-the-city framework.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FOX-ERA CASINO TRIED TO DODGE 4.3 BILLION PESOS WITH A FORGED LOAN CONTRACT</u>

SHCP filed a 4,306,799,683 peso tax evasion case against Juegos del Bajío — a casino chain that got its permit under Vicente Fox with Santiago Creel as Gobernación. Notary Public No. 25 in Quintana Roo confirmed the company's 2019 loan contract was never protocolized; the witnesses to the notarization never existed. The Tribunal Administrativo nullified the fiscal credit anyway based on the fraudulent paper. Supreme Court reviews June 4. Minister Yasmín Esquivel still opposing review.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX-PETROBRAS DEEP WATER DEAL SIGNS THIS MONTH — SHEINBAUM CONFIRMS</u>

Pemex will sign a cooperation agreement with Petrobras in June for deep-water exploration, Sheinbaum confirmed today. Petrobras is "the most advanced company in the world" in deep-water extraction — the deal also covers mature fields like Cantarell. South-South energy sovereignty, no Big Oil intermediary. The model AMLO pointed toward, now operational.

🇺🇸🇮🇱 <u>TRUMP TO NETANYAHU: "YOU'RE F***ING CRAZY, EVERYBODY HATES ISRAEL BECAUSE OF YOU"</u>

Axios reports Trump screamed "estás jodidamente loco" at Netanyahu during a Sunday call over the Lebanon escalation, telling him "you'd be in prison if it weren't for me." The fight: Israel was leveling entire buildings to kill single Hezbollah commanders. Netanyahu folded — called off the Beirut strike within hours. Empire still funds the genocide, but Israel's now too embarrassing to defend in public.

SILENCE: What US media skipped this week
May 27 – June 2, 2026 | 🤡

📰 While running cartel-tunnel and narco-politician stories on a daily loop, US outlets ran zero coverage of: Plan Mexico's first-year balance sheet, the new EU/Spain trade push (Spanish economy minister in Mexico City this week), the surging remittances figures, the rail/highway/energy infrastructure agenda from Sheinbaum's anniversary speech, and the cooperation framework with Brazil. 🇲🇽

For every "Mexico in chaos" frame in this week's US press, there were Mexican policy stories — most of them positive economic news — that did not earn a single English-language headline.

IEP / VISION OF HUMANITY: How Changing Drug Demand Could Reshape Violence in Mexico
May 27, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Rare honest piece: the Institute for Economics & Peace notes US overdose deaths fell from ~110,000 (2023) to ~68,000 (2025) and asks the obvious question — what does that mean for Mexican supply-side enforcement? 🇲🇽 The demand side finally enters the conversation.

The piece doesn't blame Mexico for US addiction — by itself a rarity in English-language reporting on Mexican violence.

• "Fewer Americans appear to be initiating drug use in the first place"
• "long-term reductions in violence may depend equally on broader social conditions"

10NEWS / STATESMAN / FOX: Otay Mesa "Buy 4 Less" cartel tunnel cluster
June 1-2, 2026 | 🟡

📰 One DOJ press release on a San Diego cocaine tunnel becomes a Hollywood pitch deck across 10News, Fox, Gateway Pundit, INQUIRER, NBC SD, and the Statesman — within 24 hours. 🔍 The product on offer is fear; the border is the studio.

The tunnel was discovered and seized on the US side — the cocaine never reached a public market — but every headline frames the story as a "Mexico" problem.

• "sophisticated tunnel that had lighting, ventilation, an electric rail system"
• "Cocaine is now the lifeblood of the cartels"

SEDAILY (KR): Mexico's Cartel Violence Casts Shadow Over 2026 World Cup
June 1, 2026 | 🟡

📰 South Korea's Seoul Economic Daily picks up the US cartel-World-Cup script unedited — "structural risks tied to cartel crime and missing persons remain unresolved." 🔍 The frame travels globally: Mexico isn't a co-host, it's a "shadow."

Mexico is deploying ~100,000 security personnel — more than Qatar mobilized for 2022 — but that detail appears as parenthetical reassurance, never as the headline.

• "Structural risks tied to cartel crime and missing persons remain unresolved"
• "Opportunistic crimes targeting tourists... warrant particular vigilance"

SPECTATOR: How the US is taking on Mexico's narco-politicians
June 2, 2026 | 🔴

📰 Joshua Treviño openly writes the imperial brief: US prosecution of Mexican politicians is "the real kind" of justice — i.e., not what Mexican courts deliver. 🔍 Sheinbaum's defense of sovereignty is filed under "victimhood," US extraterritoriality under "necessary management."

Treviño runs the Texas Public Policy Foundation's foreign-policy arm — a US think tank whose stated mission is to remake Mexican governance.

• "Mexico always the victim, Mexico always wronged"
• "the indicted figures are brought to justice—the real kind"
• "synthesizes state and cartels into the narco-estado"
